source: sgtestpaper.com free test papers, P5/P6 English, 2022-2025

patterns.name: Vocabulary MCQ: single-word choice
patterns.structure: A sentence with one blank; four single words of similar meaning or the same word class (verbs, adjectives, adverbs, nouns). Only one fits the collocation and nuance.
patterns.skill: Choose the word with the right meaning, strength and collocation.

distractorTraps.description: all four words mean roughly the same but differ in strength or tone
the word cannot go with the noun or verb in the sentence
the word is too formal or too casual for the context
options share a root or look alike but mean different things

patterns.name: Grammar MCQ (one blank in a sentence, four options)
patterns.structure: A single sentence with one blank; four short options, usually single words or two-word verb groups that differ by one grammar feature. Tested only through the choice of form.
patterns.skill: Choose the grammatically correct form in context.

distractorTraps.description: options are inflections of one word (tense, -ing, -ed, agreement)
options are words from one class (all prepositions, all wh-words, all conjunctions) and only one fits the clause
a plural or singular word right before the blank pulls the verb the wrong way
an option makes sense but breaks the structure, for example the wrong tense after a time marker

patterns.name: Visual-text comprehension MCQ (poster, brochure or notice, often paired with a second text)
patterns.section: Paper 2 Booklet A, Q21-25 (P6: often Q21-28)
patterns.structure: A poster, advertisement, brochure or schedule (sometimes with a short article or email as Text 2), then 5 to 8 questions on literal facts, the purpose of a feature (picture, quote, layout) and comparing the two texts.
patterns.skill: Read and interpret multimodal texts at literal, inferential and evaluative levels.

distractorTraps.description: the option is true of another part of the text, not the one asked about
the option says all or only where the text says some
the option states what the feature shows rather than why it is there
the option is true of Text 1 when Text 2 was asked about

patterns.name: Vocabulary-in-context MCQ (closest in meaning to a marked word in a passage)
patterns.structure: A short passage with five marked words or phrases, numbered. For each, choose the option closest in meaning to the marked item as used in the passage.
patterns.skill: Infer word meaning from context; recognise synonyms.

distractorTraps.description: the option is a real meaning of the word, but not the one used in this passage
the option looks like the word but means something else
the option does not fit the grammar of the sentence

patterns.name: Vocabulary MCQ: phrasal verb choice
patterns.structure: A sentence with one blank; four phrasal verbs sharing a verb (or a particle) and differing in the other part.
patterns.skill: Choose the phrasal verb whose particle gives the intended meaning.

distractorTraps.description: options share the verb; only one particle gives the intended sense
an option is right for the literal meaning but not the figurative one

patterns.name: Vocabulary MCQ: idiom or fixed-expression choice
patterns.structure: A sentence or short dialogue with one blank; four idioms or multi-word expressions. The context implies the intended meaning.
patterns.skill: Choose the idiom that matches the situation.

distractorTraps.description: all four idioms use a similar image (body parts, animals, money) but mean different things
one option means the opposite of what the situation needs
an option sounds plausible if read literally

patterns.name: Passage comprehension MCQ (non-visual text in Booklet A)
patterns.structure: A continuous text (article, story or email) followed by multiple-choice questions on facts, inference and the writer's purpose. Seen mainly in older papers or some schools.
patterns.skill: Show literal and inferential understanding of a written text.

distractorTraps.description: the option is true in the text but does not answer the question
the option goes further than the text

patterns.name: Cloze MCQ (numbered blanks in a passage, four options each)
patterns.section: Paper 2 Booklet A or WA papers
patterns.structure: A passage with numbered blanks; each blank has four options. Rare compared with the one-sentence formats.
patterns.skill: Use cohesion and sentence-level grammar across a passage.

distractorTraps.description: the answer depends on a clue in another sentence
options are of one word class
